lessons.rule: Re-check herdr session ownership under the board writer lock at mutation time, not only before an external herdr call.
lessons.why: T-093 R3 review reproduced two races: a foreign hook consumed an inventory after the owner bound and dispatched during its `pane list` call, and a launch reservation was persisted after another socket had bound the store. A pre-call ownership check alone was insufficient; the reviewer required an event-barrier regression for the interleaving.

lessons.rule: A foreign-session hook or sync must be a complete no-op; regressions assert unchanged task, state, events, observations and review capacity.
lessons.why: T-093 criterion 1 required foreign hooks and syncs to be successful no-ops. The R3 review found a foreign hook could set an owner task to needs_me/blocked and that a gate-only run released capacity and appended `review_released`, despite passing worker-path tests.

lessons.rule: Persist and check launch-socket ownership for every launched pane, including gate-only and reviewer launches with no worker pane.
lessons.why: In T-093 R3, `open_run_pane` returned the launch socket but `gate_start` kept only `pane_id`, so a run with `run.herdr == None` held a server-scoped gate pane that any session inventory could classify as lost. Old gate refs without a socket should be treated as unknown provenance, not as an unowned store.

lessons.rule: Write concurrency and grace-period regressions with fake herdr servers, socket/event barriers and explicit fixture timestamps, never sleeps or zero grace.
lessons.why: The accepted T-093 R3 reproducers used two fake server identities and a unix-socket barrier rather than sleeps; an intermediate fixture using zero startup grace was rejected by config validation and replaced by explicit timestamps.

lessons.rule: Map each acceptance criterion to its own regression, including auxiliary and automatic-admission variants; a passing gate does not prove criteria.
lessons.why: T-093 R3 had a passing hermetic gate (1,300 tests, all files under 800 SLOC), but the reviewer still returned changes because an external reproducer showed the gate-only variant of criterion 1 and 2 failing; "a green gate does not discharge the reproduced semantic gap." T-177 R1 independently reproduced the same coverage gap: manual sibling/dependent Plan workflows and the full gate passed, but automatic Backlog admission could not initialize a new target with an already-integrated external prerequisite. This is recurrence across two tasks, not independent evidence from each duplicated note or verdict event.

lessons.rule: Distinguish an unclaimed Plan target eligible for initialization from a deleted owned ref, so automatic Backlog admission can reach checked initialization.
lessons.why: T-177 R1 reproduced an admission deadlock: readiness rejected every missing integration ref before dispatch could initialize a new target, even though the external prerequisite had been accepted onto the proposed initial base. Explicit dispatch and Ready admission passed. Preserve missing-owned-ref refusal and final receipt/ancestry and exact-base checks; the single reviewed failure supports this narrow lifecycle rule.

lessons.rule: When reconciling Plan-target dispatch and launch changes, preserve immutable execution snapshots alongside target-base selection and final dependency checks, then gate the integrated candidate.
lessons.why: T-177 R1 had a genuine historical gate pass but conflicted with current main in dispatch.rs and launch.rs. Main added execution-snapshot capture and validation at the same boundaries as Plan-target base/dependency checks; the reviewer required retaining both invariants and fresh gate/live evidence for the resolved tree. One review supports this targeted integration lesson, not a repository-wide claim about conflicts.

lessons.rule: Test Plan landing recovery by persisting real journal boundaries, advancing real Git, reopening the store and reconciling repeatedly while asserting exactly one receipt and event.
lessons.why: T-177 R1 independently passed 13 journal tests covering Git-update-before-receipt, receipt-before-publication and event-before-ack boundaries. The reviewer identified persisted boundary simulation, rather than a timed process kill, as evidence for exactly-once recovery. This is one successful task, so confidence remains modest.

lessons.rule: For Plan-target safety refusals, assert preserved refs and worktree/index bytes or retained unpublished intent, rather than only an error string.
lessons.why: T-177 R1 independently exercised real-Git target and journal tests for external movement, wrong ownership and dirty integration checkouts. The review credited unchanged refs/files or retained intent, and staged, unstaged, untracked and index-byte preservation, as the safety evidence. These are observations from one task, not repeated independent incidents.
